story_clusters.headline: ASIO pushes to make expanded surveillance powers permanent
story_clusters.summary: Australia's domestic intelligence agency is seeking to remove sunset clauses on compulsory questioning powers introduced after 9/11. Critics warn this represents a shift toward permanent police state powers without adequate parliamentary oversight or public debate.

story_clusters.headline: RBA expected to hike rates again amid persistent inflation pressures
story_clusters.summary: Economists predict the Reserve Bank may raise the cash rate to 4.35% at its May meeting as inflation remains sticky and oil crisis adds to price pressures. The central bank has already delivered back-to-back rate hikes to 4.10% in February and March amid concerns about economic overheating.

story_clusters.headline: Government launches $20 million fuel conservation advertising campaign
story_clusters.summary: The federal government rolled out a multi-million dollar ad campaign encouraging Australians to reduce car use as the global oil crisis persists. Opposition leader Angus Taylor criticized the spending as 'propaganda' and called for greater transparency through a fuel security dashboard.
